says: The stage never says that the choice between 'Windows applies the policy' and 'the program writes the live registry itself' rests on an allow-list of edition codes. SystemInfo.HasGroupPolicyInfrastructure returns false for any code not in the list, including a failed GetProductInfo (0) and any edition added later, and PolicyLoader.Save then writes the difference into HKLM/HKCU directly and broadcasts a settings change instead of invoking RefreshPolicyEx; Main_Shown also offers the ADMX download on that result. State this as a decision-changing failure mode of the edition check (single point), with the unknown-edition reach.

Opening a LocalRegistry policy source is a write to the live registry, and it happens at every start with the saved source. PolicyLoader.New calls CreateSubKey on the typed or saved path under HKCU, HKU or HKLM (creating the key if absent) and OpenSource writes then deletes a test value under Software\Policies to learn writability. Nothing in the stage tells the person that merely opening or restoring a registry source mutates the registry; add it where sources are opened, with the startup restore in Main_Load.

The unsigned, unpinned download is told, but the stage never states the consequence after a failed run: Process 'Failed to <phase>' is the only report, the package folder name and release are constants (DownloadAdmx 3-4), and a missing en-US folder for non-English cultures (line 110, EnumerateFiles on a missing directory) throws after the destination's ownership was changed and files were already replaced. If kept as one record it should cover that the destination can be left half-updated with ownership changed (the move happens after takeOwnership), and not repeat it per technology.
